purchases.title: AI & the Architecture of Attention
purchases.summary: Nine essays circling a single anxiety: what happens to human knowing when the tools for knowing become autonomous? From prediction markets and moral hazard, through the oracle problem, to AI as coroner rather than killer. The final essay — uploading Kierkegaard to an AI and discovering the machine asked something he hadn't thought to ask himself. The conclusion: AI is not the threat. Formation is the issue.

'The Choices We Call Necessity' — the Devil Wears Prada essay — is the sharpest piece in the corpus: Hannah Arendt meets Miranda Priestly, and the argument is that moral drift doesn't announce itself. You just stop noticing what you're becoming.
